Routing rule matcher for model-to-adapter dispatch.\n//!\n//! Provides pattern matching logic for routing rules: regex/glob patterns\n//! against model names, first-match-wins semantics, and default fallback.\n\nuse crate::config::RoutingRule;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\n/// Compiled routing rule with cached regex for efficient matching.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\nstruct CompiledRule {\n    /// Compiled regex matcher.\n    matcher: Arc<regex::Regex>,\n    /// Adapter to use on match.\n    adapter: String,\n}\n\nimpl CompiledRule {\n    /// Compile a routing rule into an efficient matcher.\n    ///\n    /// Supports both regex patterns (any valid regex) and glob-style patterns:\n    /// - `*` matches any single path segment (non-greedy `[^/]+`)\n    /// - `**` matches zero or more path segments (`.+?` with greedy quantifier)\n    /// - Literal `*` or `**` must be escaped as `\\*` or `\\*\\*`\n    fn from_rule(rule: &RoutingRule) -> Result<Self, regex::Error> {\n        let pattern = &rule.match_model;\n        let adapter = rule.adapter.clone();\n\n        // Convert glob patterns to regex if needed.\n        // If the pattern contains * or ** without proper regex escaping,\n        // treat it as a glob pattern and convert.\n        let regex_pattern = if needs_glob_conversion(pattern) {\n            convert_glob_to_regex(pattern)\n        } else {\n            pattern.clone()\n        };\n\n        let matcher = regex::Regex::new(&regex_pattern)?;\n\n        Ok(CompiledRule {\n            matcher: Arc::new(matcher),\n            adapter,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Test if a model name matches this rule.\n    fn matches(&self, model: &str) -> bool {\n        self.matcher.is_match(model)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Check if a pattern contains glob-style wildcards that need conversion.\n///\n/// Returns true if the pattern appears to be a glob pattern rather than\n/// a well-formed regex. The heuristic checks for:\n/// 1. Regex features: anchors (^$), character classes [], parentheses (),\n///    quantifiers +?{}, alternation |, or the regex wildcard sequence .*\n/// 2. If present, it's a regex pattern - no conversion needed\n/// 3. If absent, but * is present, it's a glob pattern - convert it\nfn needs_glob_conversion(pattern: &str) -> bool {\n    // First, check if it looks like a regex by looking for regex metacharacters.\n    // The key indicator is .* which is \"any character\" in regex but not in glob.\n    let has_regex_features = pattern.contains(|c| {\n        matches!(\n            c,\n            '^' | '$' | '(' | ')' | '[' | ']' | '{' | '}' | '+' | '?' | '|' | '\\\\'\n        )\n    }) || pattern.contains(\".*\");\n\n    if has_regex_features {\n        // Has clear regex features - treat as regex\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    // At this point, we have a simple pattern that might be glob or regex.\n    // If it contains unescaped * (and we already ruled out other regex chars),\n    // treat it as a glob pattern.\n    let chars: Vec<char> = pattern.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        if chars[i] == '\\\\' && i + 1 < chars.len() {\n            // Skip escaped character.\n            i += 2;\n            continue;\n        }\n        if chars[i] == '*' {\n            return true;\n        }\n        i += 1;\n    }\n\n    false\n}\n\n/// Convert glob-style pattern to regex.\n///\n/// Rules:\n/// - `*` alone → `.*` (match anything, catch-all)\n/// - `*` in other contexts → `[^/]+` (match any single segment, no slashes)\n/// - `**` → `.*` (match any characters including slashes, greedy)\n/// - Escaped `\\*` and `\\*\\*` treated literally\n/// - No implicit start anchor for glob patterns (unlike regex patterns)\nfn convert_glob_to_regex(glob: &str) -> String {\n    // Special case: * and ** should match anything (including empty).\n    if glob == \"*\" || glob == \"**\" {\n        return \"^.*$\".to_string();\n    }\n\n    let mut result = String::new();\n    let chars: Vec<char> = glob.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        match chars[i] {\n            '\\\\' => {\n                // Escaped character - pass through the backslash and the character.\n                // This ensures that \\* in the glob becomes \\* in the regex (literal asterisk).\n                if i + 1 < chars.len() {\n                    result.push('\\\\');\n                    result.push(chars[i + 1]);\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    // Trailing backslash - treat literally.\n                    result.push('\\\\');\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            '*' => {\n                // Check for **.\n                if i + 1 < chars.len() && chars[i + 1] == '*' {\n                    // ** matches any characters including slashes.\n                    result.push_str(\".*\");\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    // * matches any non-slash characters.\n                    result.push_str(\"[^/]+\");\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            c => {\n                // Pass through regex metacharacters literally - regex::Regex::new\n                // will handle escaping. We only need to escape backslashes for\n                // the glob conversion.\n                result.push(c);\n                i += 1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Only add end anchor, not start anchor (glob patterns match substrings).\n    format!(\"{}$\", result)\n}\n\n/// Match a model name against routing rules, returning the adapter to use.\n///\n/// Evaluates rules in order; the first matching rule determines the adapter.\n/// If no rule matches, returns the default adapter.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `model` - The model name to match (e.g., \"claude-sonnet-4-6\").\n/// * `rules` - Ordered list of routing rules (first match wins).\n/// * `default` - Fallback adapter when no rules match.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Some(adapter)` - The adapter name to use.\n/// * `None` - No rule matched and default is empty/invalid (caller should handle).\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::routing::match_adapter;\n/// use needle::config::RoutingRule;\n///\n/// let rules = vec![\n///     RoutingRule {\n///         match_model: \"sonnet.*\".to_string(),\n///         adapter: \"claude-print\".to_string(),\n///     },\n///     RoutingRule {\n///         match_model: \"*\".to_string(),\n///         adapter: \"default-adapter\".to_string(),\n///     },\n/// ];\n///\n/// // First rule matches.\n/// assert_eq!(\n///     match_adapter(\"sonnet-4-6\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n///     Some(\"claude-print\".to_string())\n/// );\n///\n/// // Second rule (catch-all) matches.\n/// assert_eq!(\n///     match_adapter(\"other-model\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n///     Some(\"default-adapter\".to_string())\n/// );\n/// ```\npub fn match_adapter(model: &str, rules: &[RoutingRule], default: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    // Compile rules and test in order (first match wins).\n    for rule in rules {\n        match CompiledRule::from_rule(rule) {\n            Ok(compiled) => {\n                if compiled.matches(model) {\n                    return Some(compiled.adapter.clone());\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                // Log the error but continue with other rules.\n                // Invalid patterns are skipped rather than failing the entire dispatch.\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    pattern = %rule.match_model,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"invalid routing pattern — skipping rule\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // No rule matched — use default if provided.\n    if default.is_empty() {\n        None\n    } else {\n        Some(default.to_string())\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::config::RoutingRule;\n\n    fn make_rule(pattern: &str,       assert_eq!(\n            match_adapter(\"claude-sonnet-4-6\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n            Some(\"claude-print\".to_string())\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Where a configuration value originated.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ConfigSource {\n    /// Built-in default value.\n    Default,\n    /// Global config file (`~/.config/needle/config.yaml`).\n    GlobalFile(PathBuf),\n    /// Workspace config file (`.needle.yaml`).\n    WorkspaceFile(PathBuf),\n    /// Environment variable override.\n    EnvVar(String),\n    /// CLI argument override.\n    CliOverride,\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for ConfigSource {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            ConfigSource::Default => write!(f, \"built-in default\"),\n            ConfigSource::GlobalFile(p) => write!(f, \"{}\", p.display()),\n            ConfigSource::WorkspaceFile(p) => write!(f, \"{}\", p.display()),\n            ConfigSource::EnvVar(name) => write!(f, \"{} env var\", name),\n            ConfigSource::CliOverride => write!(f, \"CLI argument\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Map of config field paths to their source.\n///\n/// Used by `needle config --dump --show-source` to annotate each value.\npub type SourceMap = BTreeMap<String, ConfigSource>;\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Workspace Overrides\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Top-level Config\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Fully resolved NEEDLE configuration.\n///\n/// Loaded once at boot, immutable during a session.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct Config {\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub agent: AgentConfig,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub worker: WorkerConfig,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub workspace: WorkspaceConfig,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub strands: StrandsConfig,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub telemetry: TelemetryConfig,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub prompt: PromptConfig,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub health: HealthConfig,\n    /// Provider/model concurrency and rate limits.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub limits: LimitsConfig,\n    /// Per-model token pricing (USD per million tokens).\n    #[serde(default = \"crate::cost::default_pricing\")]\n    pub pricing: PricingConfig,\n    /// Daily budget thresholds for cost enforcement.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub budget: BudgetConfig,\n    /// Verification commands run after agent success, before accepting closure.\n    /// Legacy format — prefer `gates` for new configurations.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub verification: Vec<String>,\n    /// Pluggable validation gates.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub gates: Vec<GateConfig>,\n    /// Self-modification (hot-reload) configuration.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub self_modification: SelfModificationConfig,\n    /// FABRIC live dashboard forwarding.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub fabric: FabricConfig,\n    /// Supervisor detection configuration.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub supervisor: SupervisorConfig,\n}\n\nimpl Config {\n    /// Expand all tilde (~) paths to absolute paths using $HOME.\n    ///\n    /// This must be called after deserialization to ensure all paths\n    /// like `~/.needle` are expanded to `/home/user/.needle`.\n    /// Paths without tildes are left unchanged.\n    pub fn expand_tildes(&mut self) {\n        // workspace section\n        self.workspace.default = expand_tilde(&self.workspace.default);\n        self.workspace.home = expand_tilde(&self.workspace.home);\n\n        // agent section\n        self.agent.adapters_dir = expand_tilde(&self.agent.adapters_dir);\n\n        // strands.explore section\n        self.strands.explore.workspace_root = expand_tilde(&self.strands.explore.workspace_root);\n        self.strands.explore.workspaces = expand_tilde_vec(&self.strands.explore.workspaces);\n\n        // strands.weave section\n        self.strands.weave.exclude_workspaces =\n            expand_tilde_vec(&self.strands.weave.exclude_workspaces);\n\n        // strands.splice section\n        self.strands.splice.report_workspace =\n            expand_tilde_option(&self.strands.splice.report_workspace);\n\n        // strands.pulse.scanners[].command paths are strings, not PathBuf, so skip\n\n        // strands.reflect section - no PathBuf fields\n\n        // strands.learning section\n        self.strands.learning.global_learnings_file =\n            expand_tilde(&self.strands.learning.global_learnings_file);\n\n        // telemetry section\n        if let Some(ref mut log_dir) = self.telemetry.file_sink.log_dir {\n            *log_dir = expand_tilde(log_dir);\n        }\n\n        // health section\n        self.health.heartbeat_dir = expand_tilde_option(&self.health.heartbeat_dir);\n\n        // supervisor section\n        self.supervisor.heartbeat_path = expand_tilde_option(&self.supervisor.heartbeat_path);\n        self.supervisor.socket_path = expand_tilde_option(&self.supervisor.socket_path);\n\n        // prompt section\n        self.prompt.context_files = expand_tilde_vec(&self.prompt.context_files);\n\n        // self_modification section\n        self.self_modification.canary_workspace =\n            expand_tilde(&self.self_modification.canary_workspace);\n\n        // prompt.variants[].content_file\n        for variants in self.prompt.variants.values_mut() {\n            for variant in variants {\n                variant.content_file = expand_tilde(&variant.content_file);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Config validation\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A single config validation error.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct ConfigError {\n    /// Dot-separated field path (e.g., `agent.default`).\n    pub field: String,\n    /// Human-readable explanation.\n    pub message: String,\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for ConfigError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        write!(f, \"{}: {}\", self.field, self.message)\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// CLI overrides\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// CLI-level overrides applied after all file-based config loading.\n#[derive(Debug, Default)]\npub struct CliOverrides {\n    pub workspace: Option<PathBuf>,\n    pub worker_name: Option<String>,\n    pub agent_binary: Option<String>,\n    pub max_workers: Option<u32>,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ConfigLoader\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Loads and validates NEEDLE configuration.\npub struct ConfigLoader;\n\nimpl ConfigLoader {\n    /// Load global config from `~/.config/needle/config.yaml`.\n    ///\n    /// If the file does not exist, returns the default config (not an error).\n    pub fn load_global() -> Result<Config> {\n        let path = dirs_or_home(\".config/needle/config.yaml\");\n        Self::load_from_path(&path)\n    }\n\n    /// Load config from a specific path.\n    ///\n    /// If the file does not exist, returns the default config.\n    pub fn load_from_path(path: &Path) -> Result<Config> {\n        if !path.exists() {\n            let mut config = Config::default();\n            config.expand_tildes();\n            return Ok(config);\n        }\n        let text = std::fs::read_to_string(path)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read config file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n        let mut config: Config = serde_yaml::from_str(&text)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid YAML in Routing rule matcher for model-to-adapter dispatch.\n//!\n//! Provides pattern matching logic for routing rules: regex/glob patterns\n//! against model names, first-match-wins semantics, and default fallback.\n\nuse crate::config::RoutingRule;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\n/// Compiled routing rule with cached regex for efficient matching.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\nstruct CompiledRule {\n    /// Compiled regex matcher.\n    matcher: Arc<regex::Regex>,\n    /// Adapter to use on match.\n    adapter: String,\n}\n\nimpl CompiledRule {\n    /// Compile a routing rule into an efficient matcher.\n    ///\n    /// Supports both regex patterns (any valid regex) and glob-style patterns:\n    /// - `*` matches any single path segment (non-greedy `[^/]+`)\n    /// - `**` matches zero or more path segments (`.+?` with greedy quantifier)\n    /// - Literal `*` or `**` must be escaped as `\\*` or `\\*\\*`\n    fn from_rule(rule: &RoutingRule) -> Result<Self, regex::Error> {\n        let pattern = &rule.match_model;\n        let adapter = rule.adapter.clone();\n\n        // Convert glob patterns to regex if needed.\n        // If the pattern contains * or ** without proper regex escaping,\n        // treat it as a glob pattern and convert.\n        let regex_pattern = if needs_glob_conversion(pattern) {\n            convert_glob_to_regex(pattern)\n        } else {\n            pattern.clone()\n        };\n\n        let matcher = regex::Regex::new(&regex_pattern)?;\n\n        Ok(CompiledRule {\n            matcher: Arc::new(matcher),\n            adapter,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Test if a model name matches this rule.\n    fn matches(&self, model: &str) -> bool {\n        self.matcher.is_match(model)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Check if a pattern contains glob-style wildcards that need conversion.\n///\n/// Returns true if the pattern appears to be a glob pattern rather than\n/// a well-formed regex. The heuristic checks for:\n/// 1. Regex features: anchors (^$), character classes [], parentheses (),\n///    quantifiers +?{}, alternation |, or the regex wildcard sequence .*\n/// 2. If present, it's a regex pattern - no conversion needed\n/// 3. If absent, but * is present, it's a glob pattern - convert it\nfn needs_glob_conversion(pattern: &str) -> bool {\n    // First, check if it looks like a regex by looking for regex metacharacters.\n    // The key indicator is .* which is \"any character\" in regex but not in glob.\n    let has_regex_features = pattern.contains(|c| {\n        matches!(\n            c,\n            '^' | '$' | '(' | ')' | '[' | ']' | '{' | '}' | '+' | '?' | '|' | '\\\\'\n        )\n    }) || pattern.contains(\".*\");\n\n    if has_regex_features {\n        // Has clear regex features - treat as regex\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    // At this point, we have a simple pattern that might be glob or regex.\n    // If it contains unescaped * (and we already ruled out other regex chars),\n    // treat it as a glob pattern.\n    let chars: Vec<char> = pattern.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        if chars[i] == '\\\\' && i + 1 < chars.len() {\n            // Skip escaped character.\n            i += 2;\n            continue;\n        }\n        if chars[i] == '*' {\n            return true;\n        }\n        i += 1;\n    }\n\n    false\n}\n\n/// Convert glob-style pattern to regex.\n///\n/// Rules:\n/// - `*` alone → `.*` (match anything, catch-all)\n/// - `*` in other contexts → `[^/]+` (match any single segment, no slashes)\n/// - `**` → `.*` (match any characters including slashes, greedy)\n/// - Escaped `\\*` and `\\*\\*` treated literally\n/// - No implicit start anchor for glob patterns (unlike regex patterns)\nfn convert_glob_to_regex(glob: &str) -> String {\n    // Special case: * and ** should match anything (including empty).\n    if glob == \"*\" || glob == \"**\" {\n        return \"^.*$\".to_string();\n    }\n\n    let mut result = String::new();\n    let chars: Vec<char> = glob.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        match chars[i] {\n            '\\\\' => {\n                // Escaped character - pass through the backslash and the character.\n                // This ensures that \\* in the glob becomes \\* in the regex (literal asterisk).\n                if i + 1 < chars.len() {\n                    result.push('\\\\');\n                    result.push(chars[i + 1]);\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    // Trailing backslash - treat literally.\n                    result.push('\\\\');\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            '*' => {\n                // Check for **.\n                if i + 1 < chars.len() && chars[i + 1] == '*' {\n                    // ** matches any characters including slashes.\n                    result.push_str(\".*\");\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    // * matches any non-slash characters.\n                    result.push_str(\"[^/]+\");\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            c => {\n                // Pass through regex metacharacters literally - regex::Regex::new\n                // will handle escaping. We only need to escape backslashes for\n                // the glob conversion.\n                result.push(c);\n                i += 1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Only add end anchor, not start anchor (glob patterns match substrings).\n    format!(\"{}$\", result)\n}\n\n/// Match a model name against routing rules, returning the adapter to use.\n///\n/// Evaluates rules in order; the first matching rule determines the adapter.\n/// If no rule matches, returns the default adapter.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `model` - The model name to match (e.g., \"claude-sonnet-4-6\").\n/// * `rules` - Ordered list of routing rules (first match wins).\n/// * `default` - Fallback adapter when no rules match.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Some(adapter)` - The adapter name to use.\n/// * `None` - No rule matched and default is empty/invalid (caller should handle).\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::routing::match_adapter;\n/// use needle::config::RoutingRule;\n///\n/// let rules = vec![\n///     RoutingRule {\n///         match_model: \"sonnet.*\".to_string(),\n///         adapter: \"claude-print\".to_string(),\n///     },\n///     RoutingRule {\n///         match_model: \"*\".to_string(),\n///         adapter: \"default-adapter\".to_string(),\n///     },\n/// ];\n///\n/// // First rule matches.\n/// assert_eq!(\n///     match_adapter(\"sonnet-4-6\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n///     Some(\"claude-print\".to_string())\n/// );\n///\n/// // Second rule (catch-all) matches.\n/// assert_eq!(\n///     match_adapter(\"other-model\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n///     Some(\"default-adapter\".to_string())\n/// );\n/// ```\npub fn match_adapter(model: &str, rules: &[RoutingRule], default: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    // Compile rules and test in order (first match wins).\n    for rule in rules {\n        match CompiledRule::from_rule(rule) {\n            Ok(compiled) => {\n                if compiled.matches(model) {\n                    return Some(compiled.adapter.clone());\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                // Log the error but continue with other rules.\n                // Invalid patterns are skipped rather than failing the entire dispatch.\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    pattern = %rule.match_model,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"invalid routing pattern — skipping rule\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // No rule matched — use default if provided.\n    if default.is_empty() {\n        None\n    } else {\n        Some(default.to_string())\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests\n// Routing rule matcher for model-to-adapter dispatch.\n//!\n//! Provides pattern matching logic for routing rules: regex/glob patterns\n//! against model names, first-match-wins semantics, and default fallback.\n\nuse crate::config::RoutingRule;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse std::path::Path;\n\n/// Compiled routing rule with cached regex for efficient matching.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\nstruct CompiledRule {\n    /// Compiled regex matcher.\n    matcher: Arc<regex::Regex>,\n    /// Adapter to use on match.\n    adapter: String,\n}\n\nimpl CompiledRule {\n    /// Compile a routing rule into an efficient matcher.\n    ///\n    /// Supports both regex patterns (any valid regex) and glob-style patterns:\n    /// - `*` matches any single path segment (non-greedy `[^/]+`)\n    /// - `**` matches zero or more path segments (`.+?` with greedy quantifier)\n    /// - Literal `*` or `**` must be escaped as `\\*` or `\\*\\*`\n    fn from_rule(rule: &RoutingRule) -> Result<Self, regex::Error> {\n        let pattern = &rule.match_model;\n        let adapter = rule.adapter.clone();\n\n        // Convert glob patterns to regex if needed.\n        // If the pattern contains * or ** without proper regex escaping,\n        // treat it as a glob pattern and convert.\n        let regex_pattern = if needs_glob_conversion(pattern) {\n            convert_glob_to_regex(pattern)\n        } else {\n            pattern.clone()\n        };\n\n        let matcher = regex::Regex::new(&regex_pattern)?;\n\n        Ok(CompiledRule {\n            matcher: Arc::new(matcher),\n            adapter,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Test if a model name matches this rule.\n    fn matches(&self, model: &str) -> bool {\n        self.matcher.is_match(model)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Check if a pattern contains glob-style wildcards that need conversion.\n///\n/// Returns true if the pattern appears to be a glob pattern rather than\n/// a well-formed regex. The heuristic checks for:\n/// 1. Regex features: anchors (^$), character classes [], parentheses (),\n///    quantifiers +?{}, alternation |, or the regex wildcard sequence .*\n/// 2. If present, it's a regex pattern - no conversion needed\n/// 3. If absent, but * is present, it's a glob pattern - convert it\nfn needs_glob_conversion(pattern: &str) -> bool {\n    // First, check if it looks like a regex by looking for regex metacharacters.\n    // The key indicator is .* which is \"any character\" in regex but not in glob.\n    let has_regex_features = pattern.contains(|c| {\n        matches!(\n            c,\n            '^' | '$' | '(' | ')' | '[' | ']' | '{' | '}' | '+' | '?' | '|' | '\\\\'\n        )\n    }) || pattern.contains(\".*\");\n\n    if has_regex_features {\n        // Has clear regex features - treat as regex\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    // At this point, we have a simple pattern that might be glob or regex.\n    // If it contains unescaped * (and we already ruled out other regex chars),\n    // treat it as a glob pattern.\n    let chars: Vec<char> = pattern.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        if chars[i] == '\\\\' && i + 1 < chars.len() {\n            // Skip escaped character.\n            i += 2;\n            continue;\n        }\n        if chars[i] == '*' {\n            return true;\n        }\n        i += 1;\n    }\n\n    false\n}\n\n/// Convert glob-style pattern to regex.\n///\n/// Rules:\n/// - `*` alone → `.*` (match anything, catch-all)\n/// - `*` in other contexts → `[^/]+` (match any single segment, no slashes)\n/// - `**` → `.*` (match any characters including slashes, greedy)\n/// - Escaped `\\*` and `\\*\\*` treated literally\n/// - No implicit start anchor for glob patterns (unlike regex patterns)\nfn convert_glob_to_regex(glob: &str) -> String {\n    // Special case: * and ** should match anything (including empty).\n    if glob == \"*\" || glob == \"**\" {\n        return \"^.*$\".to_string();\n    }\n\n    let mut result = String::new();\n    let chars: Vec<char> = glob.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        match chars[i] {\n            '\\\\' => {\n                // Escaped character - pass through the backslash and the character.\n                // This ensures that \\* in the glob becomes \\* in the regex (literal asterisk).\n                if i + 1 < chars.len() {\n                    result.push('\\\\');\n                    result.push(chars[i + 1]);\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    // Trailing backslash - treat literally.\n                    result.push('\\\\');\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            '*' => {\n                // Check for **.\n                if i + 1 < chars.len() && chars[i + 1] == '*' {\n                    // ** matches any characters including slashes.\n                    result.push_str(\".*\");\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    // * matches any non-slash characters.\n                    result.push_str(\"[^/]+\");\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            c => {\n                // Pass through regex metacharacters literally - regex::Regex::new\n                // will handle escaping. We only need to escape backslashes for\n                // the glob conversion.\n                result.push(c);\n                i += 1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Only add end anchor, not start anchor (glob patterns match substrings).\n    format!(\"{}$\", result)\n}\n\n/// Match a model name against routing rules, returning the adapter to use.\n///\n/// Evaluates rules in order; the first matching rule determines the adapter.\n/// If no rule matches, returns the default adapter.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `model` - The model name to match (e.g., \"claude-sonnet-4-6\").\n/// * `rules` - Ordered list of routing rules (first match wins).\n/// * `default` - Fallback adapter when no rules match.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Some(adapter)` - The adapter name to use.\n/// * `None` - No rule matched and default is empty/invalid (caller should handle).\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::routing::match_adapter;\n/// use needle::config::RoutingRule;\n///\n/// let rules = vec![\n///     RoutingRule {\n///         match_model: \"sonnet.*\".to_string(),\n///         adapter: \"claude-print\".to_string(),\n///     },\n///     RoutingRule {\n///         match_model: \"*\".to_string(),\n///         adapter: \"default-adapter\".to_string(),\n///     },\n/// ];\n///\n/// // First rule matches.\n/// assert_eq!(\n///     match_adapter(\"sonnet-4-6\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n///     Some(\"claude-print\".to_string())\n/// );\n///\n/// // Second rule (catch-all) matches.\n/// assert_eq!(\n///     match_adapter(\"other-model\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n///     Some(\"default-adapter\".to_string())\n/// );\n/// ```\npub fn match_adapter(model: &str, rules: &[RoutingRule], default: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    // Compile rules and test in order (first match wins).\n    for rule in rules {\n        match CompiledRule::from_rule(rule) {\n            Ok(compiled) => {\n                if compiled.matches(model) {\n                    return Some(compiled.adapter.clone());\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                // Log the error but continue with other rules.\n                // Invalid patterns are skipped rather than failing the entire dispatch.\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    pattern = %rule.match_model,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"invalid routing pattern — skipping rule\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // No rule matched — use default if provided.\n    if default.is_empty() {\n        None\n    } else {\n        Some(default.to_string())\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests\n// Routing rule matcher for model-to-adapter dispatch.\n//!\n//! Provides pattern matching logic for routing rules: regex/glob patterns\n//! against model names, first-match-wins semantics, and default fallback.\n\nuse crate::config::RoutingRule;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse std::path::Path;\n\n/// Compiled routing rule with cached regex for efficient matching.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\nstruct CompiledRule {\n    /// Compiled regex matcher.\n    matcher: Arc<regex::Regex>,\n    /// Adapter to use on match.\n    adapter: String,\n}\n\nimpl CompiledRule {\n    /// Compile a routing rule into an efficient matcher.\n    ///\n    /// Supports both regex patterns (any valid regex) and glob-style patterns:\n    /// - `*` matches any single path segment (non-greedy `[^/]+`)\n    /// - `**` matches zero or more path segments (`.+?` with greedy quantifier)\n    /// - Literal `*` or `**` must be escaped as `\\*` or `\\*\\*`\n    fn from_rule(rule: &RoutingRule) -> Result<Self, regex::Error> {\n        let pattern = &rule.match_model;\n        let adapter = rule.adapter.clone();\n\n        // Convert glob patterns to regex if needed.\n        // If the pattern contains * or ** without proper regex escaping,\n        // treat it as a glob pattern and convert.\n        let regex_pattern = if needs_glob_conversion(pattern) {\n            convert_glob_to_regex(pattern)\n        } else {\n            pattern.clone()\n        };\n\n        let matcher = regex::Regex::new(&regex_pattern)?;\n\n        Ok(CompiledRule {\n            matcher: Arc::new(matcher),\n            adapter,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Test if a model name matches this rule.\n    fn matches(&self, model: &str) -> bool {\n        self.matcher.is_match(model)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Check if a pattern contains glob-style wildcards that need conversion.\n///\n/// Returns true if the pattern appears to be a glob pattern rather than\n/// a well-formed regex. The heuristic checks for:\n/// 1. Regex features: anchors (^$), character classes [], parentheses (),\n///    quantifiers +?{}, alternation |, or the regex wildcard sequence .*\n/// 2. If present, it's a regex pattern - no conversion needed\n/// 3. If absent, but * is present, it's a glob pattern - convert it\nfn needs_glob_conversion(pattern: &str) -> bool {\n    // First, check if it looks like a regex by looking for regex metacharacters.\n    // The key indicator is .* which is \"any character\" in regex but not in glob.\n    let has_regex_features = pattern.contains(|c| {\n        matches!(\n            c,\n            '^' | '$' | '(' | ')' | '[' | ']' | '{' | '}' | '+' | '?' | '|' | '\\\\'\n        )\n    }) || pattern.contains(\".*\");\n\n    if has_regex_features {\n        // Has clear regex features - treat as regex\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    // At this point, we have a simple pattern that might be glob or regex.\n    // If it contains unescaped * (and we already ruled out other regex chars),\n    // treat it as a glob pattern.\n    let chars: Vec<char> = pattern.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        if chars[i] == '\\\\' && i + 1 < chars.len() {\n            // Skip escaped character.\n            i += 2;\n            continue;\n        }\n        if chars[i] == '*' {\n            return true;\n        }\n        i += 1;\n    }\n\n    false\n}\n\n/// Convert glob-style pattern to regex.\n///\n/// Rules:\n/// - `*` alone → `.*` (match anything, catch-all)\n/// - `*` in other contexts → `[^/]+` (match any single segment, no slashes)\n/// - `**` → `.*` (match any characters including slashes, greedy)\n/// - Escaped `\\*` and `\\*\\*` treated literally\n/// - No implicit start anchor for glob patterns (unlike regex patterns)\nfn convert_glob_to_regex(glob: &str) -> String {\n    // Special case: * and ** should match anything (including empty).\n    if glob == \"*\" || glob == \"**\" {\n        return \"^.*$\".to_string();\n    }\n\n    let mut result = String::new();\n    let chars: Vec<char> = glob.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        match chars[i] {\n            '\\\\' => {\n                // Escaped character - pass through the backslash and the character.\n                // This ensures that \\* in the glob becomes \\* in the regex (literal asterisk).\n                if i + 1 < chars.len() {\n                    result.push('\\\\');\n                    result.push(chars[i + 1]);\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    // Trailing backslash - treat literally.\n                    result.push('\\\\');\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            '*' => {\n                // Check for **.\n                if i + 1 < chars.len() && chars[i + 1] == '*' {\n                    // ** matches any characters including slashes.\n                    result.push_str(\".*\");\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    // * matches any non-slash characters.\n                    result.push_str(\"[^/]+\");\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            c => {\n                // Pass through regex metacharacters literally - regex::Regex::new\n                // will handle escaping. We only need to escape backslashes for\n                // the glob conversion.\n                result.push(c);\n                i += 1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Only add end anchor, not start anchor (glob patterns match substrings).\n    format!(\"{}$\", result)\n}\n\n/// Match a model name against routing rules, returning the adapter to use.\n///\n/// Evaluates rules in default.is_empty() {\n        None\n    } else {\n        Some(default.to_string())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Match a model name against a single glob pattern using the glob crate.\n///\n/// This is a Routing rule matcher for model-to-adapter dispatch.\n//!\n//! Provides pattern matching logic for routing rules: regex/glob patterns\n//! against model names, first-match-wins semantics, and default fallback.\n\nuse crate::config::RoutingRule;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse std::path::Path;\n\n/// Compiled routing rule with cached regex for efficient matching.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\nstruct CompiledRule {\n    /// Compiled regex matcher.\n    matcher: Arc<regex::Regex>,\n    /// Adapter to use on match.\n    adapter: String,\n}\n\nimpl CompiledRule {\n    /// Compile a routing rule into an efficient matcher.\n    ///\n    /// Supports both regex patterns (any valid regex) and glob-style patterns:\n    /// - `*` matches any single path segment (non-greedy `[^/]+`)\n    /// - `**` matches zero or more path segments (`.+?` with greedy quantifier)\n    /// - Literal `*` or `**` must be escaped as `\\*` or `\\*\\*`\n    fn from_rule(rule: &RoutingRule) -> Result<Self, regex::Error> {\n        let pattern = &rule.match_model;\n        let adapter = rule.adapter.clone();\n\n        // Convert glob patterns to regex if needed.\n        // If the pattern contains * or ** without proper regex escaping,\n        // treat it as a glob pattern and convert.\n        let regex_pattern = if needs_glob_conversion(pattern) {\n            convert_glob_to_regex(pattern)\n        } else {\n            pattern.clone()\n        };\n\n        let matcher = regex::Regex::new(&regex_pattern)?;\n\n        Ok(CompiledRule {\n            matcher: Arc::new(matcher),\n            adapter,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Test if a model name matches this rule.\n    fn matches(&self, model: &str) -> bool {\n        self.matcher.is_match(model)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Check if a pattern contains glob-style wildcards that need conversion.\n///\n/// Returns true if the pattern appears to be a glob pattern rather than\n/// a well-formed regex. The heuristic checks for:\n/// 1. Regex features: anchors (^$), character classes [], parentheses (),\n///    quantifiers +?{}, alternation |, or the regex wildcard sequence .*\n/// 2. If present, it's a regex pattern - no conversion needed\n/// 3. If absent, but * is present, it's a glob pattern - convert it\nfn needs_glob_conversion(pattern: &str) -> bool {\n    // First, check if it looks like a regex by looking for regex metacharacters.\n    // The key indicator is .* which is \"any character\" in regex but not in glob.\n    let has_regex_features = pattern.contains(|c| {\n        matches!(\n            c,\n            '^' | '$' | '(' | ')' | '[' | ']' | '{' | '}' | '+' | '?' | '|' | '\\\\'\n        )\n    }) || pattern.contains(\".*\");\n\n    if has_regex_features {\n        // Has clear regex features - treat as regex\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    // At this point, we have a simple pattern that might be glob or regex.\n    // If it contains unescaped * (and we already ruled out other regex chars),\n    // treat it as a glob pattern.\n    let chars: Vec<char> = pattern.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        if chars[i] == '\\\\' && i + 1 < chars.len() {\n            // Skip escaped character.\n            i += 2;\n            continue;\n        }\n        if chars[i] == '*' {\n            return true;\n        }\n        i += 1;\n    }\n\n    false\n}\n\n/// Convert glob-style pattern to regex.\n///\n/// Rules:\n/// - `*` alone → `.*` (match anything, catch-all)\n/// - `*` in other contexts → `[^/]+` (match any single segment, no slashes)\n/// - `**` → `.*` (match any characters including slashes, greedy)\n/// - Escaped `\\*` and `\\*\\*` treated literally\n/// - No implicit start anchor for glob patterns (unlike regex patterns)\nfn convert_glob_to_regex(glob: &str) -> String {\n    // Special case: * and ** should match anything (including empty).\n    if glob == \"*\" || glob == \"**\" {\n        return \"^.*$\".to_string();\n    }\n\n    let mut result = String::new();\n    let chars: Vec<char> = glob.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        match chars[i] {\n            '\\\\' => {\n                // Escaped character - Routing rule matcher for model-to-adapter dispatch.\n//!\n//! Provides pattern matching logic for routing rules: regex/glob patterns\n//! against model names, first-match-wins semantics, and default fallback.\n\nuse crate::config::RoutingRule;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse std::path::Path;\n\n/// Compiled routing rule with cached regex for efficient matching.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\nstruct CompiledRule {\n    /// Compiled regex matcher.\n    matcher: Arc<regex::Regex>,\n    /// Adapter to use on match.\n    adapter: String,\n}\n\nimpl CompiledRule {\n    /// Compile a routing rule into an efficient matcher.\n    ///\n    /// Supports both regex patterns (any valid regex) and glob-style patterns:\n    /// - `*` matches any single path segment (non-greedy `[^/]+`)\n    /// - `**` matches zero or more path segments (`.+?` with greedy quantifier)\n    /// - Literal `*` or `**` must be escaped as `\\*` or `\\*\\*`\n    fn from_rule(rule: &RoutingRule) -> Result<Self, regex::Error> {\n        let pattern = &rule.match_model;\n        let adapter = rule.adapter.clone();\n\n        // Convert glob patterns to regex if needed.\n        // If the pattern contains * or ** without proper regex escaping,\n        // treat it as a glob pattern and convert.\n        let regex_pattern = if needs_glob_conversion(pattern) {\n            convert_glob_to_regex(pattern)\n        } else {\n            pattern.clone()\n        };\n\n        let matcher = regex::Regex::new(&regex_pattern)?;\n\n        Ok(CompiledRule {\n            matcher: Arc::new(matcher),\n            adapter,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Test if a model name matches this rule.\n    fn matches(&self, model: &str) -> bool {\n        self.matcher.is_match(model)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Check if a pattern contains glob-style wildcards that need conversion.\n///\n/// Returns true if the pattern appears to be a glob pattern rather than\n/// a well-formed regex. The heuristic checks for:\n/// 1. Regex features: anchors (^$), character classes [], parentheses (),\n///    quantifiers +?{}, alternation |, or the regex wildcard sequence .*\n/// 2. If present, it's a regex pattern - no conversion needed\n/// 3. If absent, but * is present, it's a glob pattern - convert it\nfn needs_glob_conversion(pattern: &str) -> bool {\n    // First, check if it looks like a regex by looking for regex metacharacters.\n    // The key indicator is .* which is \"any character\" in regex but not in glob.\n    let has_regex_features = pattern.contains(|c| {\n        matches!(\n            c,\n            '^' | '$' | '(' | ')' | '[' | ']' | '{' | '}' | '+' | '?' | '|' | '\\\\'\n        )\n    }) || pattern.contains(\".*\");\n\n    if has_regex_features {\n        // Has clear regex features - treat as regex\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    // At this point, we have a simple pattern that might be glob or regex.\n    // If it contains unescaped * (and we already ruled out other regex chars),\n    // treat it as a glob pattern.\n    let chars: Vec<char> = pattern.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        if chars[i] == '\\\\' && i + 1 < chars.len() {\n            // Skip escaped character.\n            i += 2;\n            continue;\n        }\n        if chars[i] == '*' {\n            return true;\n        }\n        i += 1;\n    }\n\n    false\n}\n\n/// Convert glob-style pattern to regex.\n///\n/// Rules:\n/// - `*` alone → `.*` (match anything, catch-all)\n/// - `*` in other contexts → `[^/]+` (match any single segment, no slashes)\n/// - `**` → `.*` (match any characters including slashes, greedy)\n/// - Escaped `\\*` and `\\*\\*` treated literally\n/// - No implicit start anchor for glob patterns (unlike regex patterns)\nfn convert_glob_to_regex(glob: &str) -> String {\n    // Special case: * and ** should match anything (including empty).\n    if glob == \"*\" || glob == \"**\" {\n        return \"^.*$\".to_string();\n    }\n\n    let mut result = String::new();\n    let chars: Vec<char> = glob.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        match chars[i] {\n            '\\\\' => {\n                // Escaped character - pass through the backslash and the character.\n                // This ensures that \\* in the glob becomes \\* in the regex (literal asterisk).\n                if i + 1 < chars.len() {\n                    result.push('\\\\');\n                    result.push(chars[i + 1]);\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    // Trailing backslash - treat literally.\n                    result.push('\\\\');\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            '*' => {\n                // Check for **.\n                if i + 1 < chars.len() && chars[i + 1] == '*' {\n                    // ** matches any characters including slashes.\n                    result.push_str(\".*\");\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    // * matches any non-slash characters.\n                    result.push_str(\"[^/]+\");\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            c => {\n                // Pass through regex metacharacters literally - regex::Regex::new\n                // will handle escaping. We only need to escape backslashes for\n                // the glob conversion.\n                result.push(c);\n                i += 1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Only add end anchor, not start anchor (glob patterns match substrings).\n    format!(\"{}$\", result)\n}\n\n/// Match a model name against routing rules, returning the adapter to use.\n///\n/// Evaluates rules in compiled.matches(model) {\n                    return Some(compiled.adapter.clone());\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                // Log the error but continue with       Some(())\n            } else {\n                None\n            }\n        }\n        Err(_) => {\n            // Invalid glob pattern\n            None\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// `pattern` - Glob pattern to match (e.g., \"claude-*\", \"gpt-*\", \"*\").\n/// * `model_name` - The model name to test against the pattern.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Some(())` - The pattern matches the model name.\n/// * `None` - The pattern does not match or is invalid.\n///\n/// # Edge Cases\n///\n/// * Empty pattern: Returns `None` (no match).\n/// * Empty model name: Returns `None` (no match).\n/// * Invalid glob pattern: Returns `None` (no match).\n///\n/// # Glob Pattern Syntax\n///\n/// * `*` - Matches any sequence of non-separator characters.\n/// * `**` - Matches any sequence of characters, including path separators.\n/// * `?` - Matches any single non-separator character.\n/// * `[a-z]` - Matches any character in the bracket.\n/// * `[!a-z]` - Matches any character not in the bracket.\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::routing::match_adapter_with_glob;\n///\n/// // Match with wildcard\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-sonnet-4-6\").is_some());\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-opus-4-6\").is_some());\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"gpt-4\").is_none());\n///\n/// // Match with double wildcard\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"**\", \"any-model\").is_some());\n///\n/// // Edge cases\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"\", \"model\").is_none());\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"pattern\", \"\").is_none());\n/// ```\npub fn match_adapter_with_glob(pattern: &str, model_name: &str) -> Option<()> {\n    // Handle edge cases\n    if pattern.is_empty() || model_name.is_empty() {\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    // Use the glob crate to compile and match the pattern\n    match glob::Pattern::new(pattern) {\n        Ok(glob_pattern) => {\n            // The glob crate's Pattern::matches takes a &str directly\n            if glob_pattern.matches(model_name) {\n                Some(())\n            } else {\n                None\n            }\n        }\n        Err(_) => {\n            // Invalid glob pattern\n            None\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n//
